hero.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets to rebuild Gulf nations
hero.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect Iranian assets to help Gulf allies recover from war damage.
hero.body:
The Treasury Department is considering removing sanctions on Iranian oil currently stranded on tankers at sea as part of efforts to control rising energy prices, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Thursday.

Bessent said the administration may lift sanctions on approximately 140 million barrels of Iranian crude in the coming days. He described the move as a temporary measure to address supply disruptions caused by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

"In essence, we will be using the Iranian barrels against the Iranians to keep the price down for the next 10 to 14 days as we continue this campaign," Bessent said during an appearance on Fox Business Network.

The oil stranded on tankers represents roughly 10 to 14 days of supply that Iran had been directing toward China. Oil prices have exceeded $100 per barrel for much of the past two weeks following Iran's actions blocking the critical shipping route and attacking vessels.

According to a source familiar with Treasury planning, the administration could implement a waiver similar to one previously used for Russian oil. Such a waiver would allow sales of crude already at sea within a limited timeframe. The source indicated that diverting oil already intended for China into broader global markets could help address supply shortages and reduce Iran's ability to leverage the strait closure.

The Treasury is also pursuing other measures to increase oil supplies. Bessent said the department would release additional stocks from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve beyond last week's coordinated G7 release of 400 million barrels. He emphasized that while the administration would not intervene in financial futures markets, it would focus on increasing physical supplies to compensate for the 10 to 14 million barrel-per-day deficit caused by the strait's closure.

However, experts have questioned whether this approach serves American interests. David Tannenbaum from Blackstone Compliance Services told the BBC that allowing Iran to sell oil could inadvertently strengthen the regime's financial position.

"Essentially, we're allowing Iran to sell oil, which could then be used to fund the war effort," Tannenbaum said.

Alex Zerden, founder of Capitol Peak Strategies, expressed similar concerns to the New York Times, arguing that Iran would likely profit from the sales.

"Iran will likely profit from these sales, thereby providing more money to fund its regime, the war and its proxies," Zerden said, adding that he doubted the measure would provide meaningful market reassurance.

Bessent's proposal represents a short-term approach to address immediate energy market disruptions, though analysts question its long-term effectiveness and potential unintended consequences.

cards.headline: Iran and Israel Exchange Strikes in First Direct Attacks Since April
cards.teaser: Iran launched waves of missiles at Israel while Israel struck military targets and a petrochemical complex in Iran.
cards.body:
Iran and Israel traded military strikes early Monday in a significant escalation that threatens to pull the wider Middle East into a full-scale conflict. Iran launched waves of missiles at Israel, marking the first direct attack since a fragile ceasefire began in early April. Israel responded by striking Iranian military targets and a petrochemical complex within Iranian territory.

The exchanges complicate ongoing mediation efforts to resolve the regional conflict. Yemen's Houthi rebels added to tensions by warning they would target Israel-affiliated ships in the Red Sea, further threatening regional stability.

cards.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iranian missile attack
cards.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to strike Iran in response to a missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy.
cards.body:
President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to strike Iran in response to a missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the call. The conversation came after Iran launched missiles at Israel earlier in the day, the first such attack since an April ceasefire.

The president's effort to restrain an Israeli response reflects his administration's concern that further military escalation could derail ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran. Trump spoke with Axios before the call and indicated he planned to urge Netanyahu to hold off on retaliation. Despite the intervention, Israel proceeded with strikes on military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning local time, according to the Israel Defense Forces.

The Israeli strikes mark a significant escalation in tensions between the two nations and represent the first time Israel has struck Iran since the April ceasefire. The IDF said the strikes targeted military facilities in retaliation for the Iranian missile attack. The exchange of fire threatens to unravel the diplomatic efforts underway between Washington and Tehran.

The Trump administration has been working to negotiate with Iran while managing the fallout from the renewed conflict. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is planning to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in rebuilding after damage from the war, according to a CBS News report citing a source aware of Bessent's thinking. The Treasury Department intends to redirect these funds to support regional partners affected by Iranian military action.

Trump has defended his handling of the situation against critics who say the conflict contradicts his campaign promise of no new wars. The president dismissed the notion that launching military action against Iran betrayed his 2024 campaign message. The ongoing negotiations and military tensions present a complex challenge for the administration as it seeks to manage both diplomatic engagement and regional security concerns.

cards.headline: Israel conducts strikes on Iranian military sites
cards.teaser: The Israeli Air Force hit military targets in central and western Iran following Tehran's missile attack.
cards.body:
The Israeli Air Force struck military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning, according to the Israel Defense Forces. The strikes came in response to Iranian missile attacks on Israel.

The exchange marked an escalation in tensions between the two countries and threatened to widen the regional conflict. The strikes occurred despite an appeal from U.S. President Donald Trump to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urging restraint. Yemen's Houthi rebels warned they would target Israel-affiliated ships in the Red Sea amid the escalating tensions.

cards.headline: Airlines Face $100 Billion Fuel Cost Increase From Oil Shock
cards.teaser: The global airline industry is confronting a massive increase in jet fuel expenses tied to energy market disruptions.
cards.body:
Airlines worldwide are facing an additional $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year as oil prices surge due to the Iran conflict. Industry officials warned that the increased expenses will likely lead to higher airfares for passengers as carriers work to offset the financial impact.

The International Air Transport Association reported on the state of the global air transport industry at its annual meeting. The organization slashed profit forecasts for 2026 as the fuel shock from the Iran energy crisis began to reshape financial projections across the sector.

cards.headline: Europe Unveils Plan to Reduce Dependence on American Technology
cards.teaser: The European Commission announced a technology sovereignty package aimed at lessening reliance on U.S. tech companies.
cards.body:
European officials introduced a comprehensive technology sovereignty initiative designed to reduce the continent's dependence on American technology companies. The package reflects growing concerns among European policymakers about strategic vulnerabilities tied to reliance on foreign technology infrastructure.

The plan includes measures to support European technology development and establish greater control over critical digital infrastructure. Officials emphasized the desire to ensure that no external parties hold what they described as a kill switch over European technological capabilities.

cards.headline: Powerful Earthquake Kills at Least 15 in Southern Philippines, Triggers Tsunami Warnings
cards.body:
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck off the southern Philippine island of Mindanao early Monday, collapsing buildings and killing at least 15 people while injuring more than 200 others. The quake's epicenter was located 8 miles southwest of General Santos City at a depth of 6.2 miles, according to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology.

The tremors caused widespread destruction across the region. At least 12 people died in the Soccsksargen region of Mindanao, while three died in Davao Occidental province. Robert Dagon, a police official in General Santos City, told Agence France-Presse that "many buildings were affected, but I cannot enumerate them now because we are busy with ongoing rescues."

Video footage verified by international news organizations documented severe damage including the collapse of the upper floor of a Jollibee restaurant in General Santos City and the outer concrete walls of a commercial complex crumbling to the ground. In Davao del Sur, part of a high school collapsed as students were gathering outside. A convenience store in General Santos City had its entire entrance destroyed, with smashed glass and overturned benches scattered across the street.

The earthquake triggered tsunami warnings across the Pacific region. The Pacific Tsunami Warning Center initially warned that waves up to 3 meters were possible on some Philippine coasts and waves up to 1 meter were possible on coasts of Indonesia and Malaysia. A later update indicated the tsunami threat had largely subsided.

The office of civil defence warned residents to avoid entering damaged homes and other infrastructure due to the risk of aftershocks. Power outages were reported across affected areas, and authorities urged people to move to higher ground as a precaution.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. confirmed that evacuation centers were ready and operational as government agencies continued assessing damage and clearing routes for rescue operations. He also ordered the suspension of schools in affected areas until further notice, saying "the safety of our children comes first." The earthquake struck as public schools were reopening for a new academic year, causing panic among students during morning flag ceremonies. The Philippines Red Cross responded to three high schools to support traumatized students.

The Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire, an arc of seismic faults around the Pacific Ocean where the majority of the world's earthquakes occur. The country is one of the world's most disaster-prone nations, regularly experiencing earthquakes and volcanic eruptions along with approximately 20 typhoons and tropical storms annually.

The full extent of casualties and damage remained unclear as rescue teams continued accessing remote and affected communities to complete their assessments.

cards.headline: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan Wins Re-election
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan was on track to win re-election despite a pressure campaign by Moscow.
cards.body:
Armenia's ruling Civil Contract party, led by Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, secured a slim majority in parliamentary elections, cementing the country's shift toward Europe and away from Russia. The victory represents a significant political realignment for the traditionally Moscow-aligned nation.

Pashinyan's re-election strengthens his push for deeper European integration despite warnings from Moscow. The opposition Strong Armenia alliance, backed by Russian-Armenian billionaire Samvel Karapetyan, won 25 percent of parliamentary seats but failed to prevent the pro-Europe party's victory.

cards.headline: Tech Stocks Drop in Asian Markets After Middle East Attacks
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan declined following renewed military strikes in the Middle East.
cards.body:
Stock markets in South Korea and Japan fell as tech stocks retreated from recent highs. The decline followed renewed military attacks in the Middle East, which raised concerns about regional stability and global economic impact. Asian markets had experienced a rally in tech stocks in recent weeks before the pullback.

The drop in tech stocks came as investors reassessed risk following the exchange of strikes between Iran and Israel. Markets in the region had been riding a wave of optimism about technology sector growth, but geopolitical tensions prompted a shift in investor sentiment. Trading reflected broader uncertainty about how escalating Middle East conflict could affect global markets.

cards.headline: Peru Presidential Runoff in Dead Heat Between Left and Right Candidates
cards.teaser: The runoff election pitted a leftist candidate against a right-wing opponent focused on crime.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential runoff election on Sunday presented voters with a stark left-right choice between Keiko Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, and leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez. Fujimori finished first in April's initial round with 17% of the vote, while Sánchez secured 12%, narrowly ahead of ultra-conservative Rafael López Aliaga.

The election came against a backdrop of rising crime, political instability, and corruption scandals that have plagued Peru for years. The country has cycled through eight presidents in a decade, leaving many voters prioritizing stability and solutions to crime and inequality. The tight race reflected deep polarization in Peruvian society as citizens weighed competing visions for addressing the nation's challenges.

cards.headline: Pope and Spanish Prime Minister Align Against Trump Policies
cards.teaser: Pope Leo XIV and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of Spain both recently clashed with President Trump.

cards.headline: North Korea Strengthens Economy Through Russia Partnership During Pandemic
cards.teaser: Kim Jong-un tightened control during the pandemic and energized the economy by leveraging Russia's war in Ukraine.
cards.body:
Kim Jong-un used the pandemic to tighten control over North Korea while simultaneously pursuing economic opportunities through closer ties with Russia. Border closures during Covid-19 allowed him to restrict information flow and limit movement within the country, strengthening his domestic grip.

North Korea's relationship with China strained during the pandemic as trade virtually froze. Instead, Pyongyang increasingly turned toward Russia, establishing a relationship that provided economic benefits to the isolated nation. This strategic shift away from its traditional ally reflected Kim's effort to diversify North Korea's international partnerships and secure resources for his economy.

hero.headline: Six people wounded in stabbing attack at Penn Station
hero.body:
Six people were injured in a knife attack at Penn Station in New York City, with a suspect taken into custody following the incident, according to law enforcement sources and news reports.

The stabbing occurred at the major transportation hub, which serves as a critical transit point for hundreds of thousands of daily commuters traveling through Manhattan on Amtrak, Long Island Rail Road, and New Jersey Transit services. Emergency responders arrived at the scene and transported the injured to nearby hospitals for treatment.

Initial reports from the Fire Department of New York indicated five injuries, though sources later confirmed that a sixth person was also wounded in the attack. The extent of injuries sustained by the victims has not been fully detailed by authorities.

Law enforcement officials arrested a suspect in connection with the stabbing. The motive behind the violence remains under investigation, and authorities have not indicated whether the attack targeted specific individuals or was random in nature.

Penn Station has experienced previous security incidents due to its high volume of foot traffic and importance as a key infrastructure point in New York City's transportation network. In recent years, the station implemented security upgrades designed to improve safety, including increased police presence and enhanced surveillance systems.

The stabbing adds to broader concerns about public safety in major transit hubs across the country. Penn Station serves as a vital connection point for the regional economy and daily commuting patterns, linking travelers from New Jersey, Long Island, and areas north of the city.

The attack disrupted normal operations at the station as police secured the area and attended to victims. First responders worked to treat and transport the injured while conducting their investigation into what led to the violence.

Authorities continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the incident. Additional details about the weapon used, the nature of the confrontation, and the identities of the victims and suspect have not been released to the public as the investigation remains ongoing.

The incident highlights ongoing challenges facing major transportation centers in managing security while accommodating the millions of passengers who pass through these facilities daily. Penn Station, as one of the nation's busiest transportation hubs, has faced repeated calls for enhanced safety measures to protect the large numbers of commuters and travelers who depend on its services.

As the investigation continues, law enforcement officials are working to gather more information about the events that led to the stabbing and to better understand the circumstances that resulted in multiple people being injured at the busy transit center in Manhattan.

cards.headline: Father and twin 10-year-old boys found dead in apparent murder-suicide in Canoga Park
cards.teaser: Police in Los Angeles are investigating the deaths of two children and an adult in what appears to be a murder-suicide shooting.
cards.body:
A father and his twin 10-year-old sons were found dead in Canoga Park in what the Los Angeles Police Department is investigating as an apparent murder-suicide. Officers discovered the three bodies after responding to a shooting call in the San Fernando Valley neighborhood.

The LAPD has not released the names of the victims or additional details about the circumstances surrounding the deaths. Canoga Park is a residential area in the northwest section of Los Angeles. Investigators are working to piece together what led to the incident.

cards.headline: Trump ends NBC interview after confrontation over election fraud claims
cards.teaser: The former president walked out of a Meet the Press interview when pressed by moderator Kristen Welker on his repeated assertions about the 2020 election.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump walked out of an NBC News interview on Meet the Press after a tense exchange with moderator Kristen Welker. The confrontation occurred when Welker repeatedly challenged Trump's claims that the 2020 presidential election and California governor's race were rigged.

The interview took place on Friday in Wisconsin and aired on Sunday. Trump's abrupt exit came during the heated discussion about his election fraud allegations and questions regarding compensation for those charged in the January 6 insurrection.

cards.headline: Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner holds Maine town hall amid allegations
cards.teaser: Platner appeared before a friendly crowd after a week of damage control in his Senate campaign, while some Democrats express reluctance about supporting him.
cards.body:
Senate candidate Graham Platner held a town hall in Portland, Maine, following a week of damage control after facing multiple allegations. The former Marine-turned-oyster farmer has been accused of sending sexually explicit messages to women while married and having a Nazi-themed tattoo.

Democratic congressman Ro Khanna offered qualified support for Platner's bid to unseat Republican Senator Susan Collins, acknowledging his actions were "misogynistic, shameful, and wrong." The allegations have created divisions within Maine's Democratic party as the November election approaches.

cards.headline: Tech stocks slide in Asia after Middle East attacks
cards.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan fell following a recent rally in technology shares and renewed military strikes in the region.
cards.body:
Technology stocks declined across Asian markets, interrupting a recent rally that had driven shares to record levels. Markets in South Korea and Japan experienced drops as investors responded to geopolitical developments in the Middle East.

The sell-off reflected a common market pattern: when geopolitical instability increases, investors typically shift away from riskier assets like technology stocks toward safer alternatives. The renewed military attacks in the region added uncertainty to global markets, reversing the sector's strong recent performance in the region.

cards.headline: M&S launches training program for 1,000 young people not in employment or education
cards.teaser: The British retailer announced a new traineeship scheme designed to address the growing number of youth outside the workforce and school system.
cards.body:
Marks & Spencer has launched a new traineeship scheme targeting 1,000 young people who are currently not in employment, education, or training. The retailer created the initiative to address what it identifies as a growing challenge facing young people across the United Kingdom.

The program will provide participants with training and work experience opportunities designed to equip them with skills for employment.

cards.headline: BBC investigation finds illegal sperm donor services targeting vulnerable women on social media
cards.teaser: A news organization paid 100 pounds for a donor's sample delivered by mail alongside a carton of passata in an undercover probe.
cards.body:
A BBC investigation has exposed illegal sperm donation services operating on social media, targeting vulnerable women seeking to conceive. Undercover reporters purchased a sperm sample for £100, which was delivered by post alongside a carton of passata.

These unregulated services operate outside licensed fertility clinics, bypassing the health screening and legal safeguards that regulated channels provide. The investigation demonstrates how donors are using social media platforms to connect directly with potential clients, creating arrangements that lack proper medical oversight and protection.

hero.headline: Asian Tech Stocks Tumble After Rally and Middle East Tensions
hero.teaser: Markets in South Korea and Japan declined after recent gains in technology shares.
hero.body:
Technology stocks across Asia fell sharply, with markets in South Korea and Japan leading the downturn. The decline followed a sustained rally in tech shares over recent weeks that had driven valuations to elevated levels.

The selloff came as renewed military strikes in the Middle East added to investor concerns about global stability. The combination of profit-taking after the extended rally and geopolitical uncertainty prompted traders to reduce exposure to technology stocks that had been market leaders.

The International Air Transport Association reported on the state of the global air transport industry at its annual meeting. The organization slashed profit forecasts for 2026 as the fuel shock from the Iran energy crisis began to reshape financial projections across the sector.

cards.headline: AI Chip Concentration Distorts Asian Stock Market Benchmarks
cards.teaser: The dominance of a few artificial intelligence chipmakers has warped investment strategies across Asian markets.
cards.body:
Major artificial intelligence chip stocks have grown so large within Asian market indexes that they are creating distortions for investment funds tracking those benchmarks. Fund managers are being forced to sell shares of top performers like TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix despite strong fundamentals, simply to maintain balanced portfolios.

The concentration of AI-related technology stocks has created a situation where active fund managers find themselves trapped in a cycle of selling during rallies. The unusual dynamic reflects how the rapid growth of a few semiconductor giants has reshaped the composition of regional equity indexes.

cards.headline: Nvidia and SK Hynix Form Multi-Year AI Chip Partnership
cards.teaser: The semiconductor companies announced a long-term agreement to develop memory technology for artificial intelligence applications.
cards.body:
Nvidia and SK Hynix signed a multi-year technology partnership focused on advancing memory chips for AI infrastructure. The agreement will see the companies collaborate on developing specialized memory solutions designed for artificial intelligence workloads and data centers.

Nvidia CEO announced that the company's new Vera chip will incorporate memory chips produced by SK Hynix. The partnership represents a significant expansion of collaboration between the AI chip leader and the South Korean memory manufacturer.

cards.headline: OPEC Plus Increases Oil Output Despite Middle East Tensions
cards.teaser: The oil cartel moved to boost production by 188,000 barrels per day as regional conflict intensifies.
cards.body:
OPEC Plus announced plans to increase oil production by 188,000 barrels per day amid ongoing Middle East tensions. The cartel's move comes as a ceasefire between Iran and Israel remains out of reach.

The production boost is considered largely symbolic given current market disruptions. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route for global oil supplies, faces potential shutdown due to escalating hostilities in the region, effectively stranding significant quantities of oil.

cards.headline: South Korean Stock Market Leads Global Decline
cards.teaser: Foreign investors dumped billions of dollars in Korean stocks despite a record market rally.
cards.body:
South Korea's stock market has experienced a significant meltdown, with foreign investors dumping billions of dollars in Korean equities this year. The selloff comes despite the market having recently reached record highs, with technology stocks hit particularly hard.

The decline reflects broader concerns about artificial intelligence-related valuations globally. As investors reassess the sustainability of the AI-driven rally, they have withdrawn capital from Korean positions, unwinding trades that had propelled the market to new peaks.

hero.headline: Astronomers identify source of mysterious repeating radio signals from space
hero.body:
Astronomers have identified the source of mysterious radio signals that have puzzled scientists for two decades. The signals originate from a binary star system consisting of a white dwarf star pulling matter from a companion star, creating what researchers describe as a vampire star feeding on its victim. The discovery was published in the journal Nature.

The repeating radio signals, which have been detected periodically over the years, come from an accreting white dwarf binary system. In such systems, a dense white dwarf star draws material from a neighboring star, creating intense magnetic fields and radiation. The research team traced the radio emissions to this stellar interaction, solving a longstanding astronomical mystery about the origin of these regular cosmic broadcasts.

A student astronomer played a key role in identifying the source of the signals. The breakthrough represents what researchers are calling their Rosetta stone for understanding this type of cosmic phenomenon. The signals arrive in regular patterns, allowing scientists to study the behavior and physics of white dwarf systems with unprecedented detail.

White dwarfs are the remnants of stars that have exhausted their nuclear fuel. When paired with another star in a binary system, they can pull gas and material from their companion, heating it to extreme temperatures and producing various forms of radiation. The radio signals detected from this system provide insight into the physical processes occurring as matter spirals onto the white dwarf's surface.

The discovery helps astronomers better understand binary star evolution and the extreme physics at work in these systems. The research also demonstrates how mysterious signals from space, once thought to be unexplainable, can be decoded through persistent observation and analysis. The findings may help scientists identify similar systems elsewhere in the galaxy and refine models of stellar behavior in compact binary pairs.

cards.headline: Nvidia announces RTX Spark chip, Microsoft unveils Surface Laptop Ultra at Computex
cards.teaser: Nvidia and Microsoft revealed new computing hardware aimed at advancing personal AI capabilities on Windows PCs.
cards.body:
Nvidia announced the RTX Spark at Computex, positioning it as the most efficient PC chip the company has built. The chip is part of a broader partnership with Microsoft to redesign Windows PCs for what the companies describe as the age of personal AI. Nvidia also revealed specifications for its N1x and N1 laptop chips.

Microsoft demonstrated the Surface Laptop Ultra at the technology conference. Industry observers suggest the new hardware represents a serious push by Microsoft in the PC market. Some analysts have compared Nvidia's RTX Spark chip to Apple's silicon in terms of its potential impact on the Windows computing ecosystem.

cards.headline: Apple prepares to announce new AI features at developer conference
cards.teaser: Apple is expected to unveil AI capabilities at its Worldwide Developers Conference, offering a second attempt at its AI rollout after previous difficulties.
cards.body:
Apple is set to present new artificial intelligence features at its WWDC event, with CEO Tim Cook leading the announcement. The presentation comes after what Reuters described as two years of difficulties in the company's AI efforts. The conference gives Apple another opportunity to demonstrate its AI strategy to developers and the public.

The keynote presentation is scheduled for release, with technology observers anticipating announcements related to Siri and other AI-powered features. Apple has held its annual developer conference to showcase software updates and new technologies for its platforms. The company faces heightened expectations as competitors have accelerated their own AI product releases.

cards.headline: NASA astronauts to wear Prada-designed gear for Artemis IV mission
cards.teaser: The space agency revealed that astronauts will wear undergarments designed by the luxury fashion house for upcoming moon missions.
cards.body:
NASA and Axiom Space have partnered with Prada to develop specialized undergarments for the Artemis IV mission. The Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) will serve as a base layer beneath the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit spacesuit, helping regulate temperature during lunar surface operations.

The collaboration marks Prada's expansion into the space industry. Astronauts will wear the Prada-designed garments when Artemis IV returns humans to the Moon in 2028.

cards.headline: Xbox announces Gears of War: E-Day launching this October
cards.teaser: Microsoft revealed the next entry in the Gears of War franchise will release as a console exclusive for Xbox Series X/S and PC.
cards.body:
Microsoft revealed Gears of War: E-Day at its Xbox Games Showcase, confirming the game will launch in October as an Xbox console and PC exclusive. The game will not be coming to PlayStation 5, despite previous speculation about a multi-platform release.

The announcement was made during a dedicated presentation for the Gears of War franchise as part of Microsoft's broader summer showcase, which featured multiple game announcements and trailers across first-party and third-party titles.

cards.headline: Sega confirms generative AI use in new Crazy Taxi game
cards.teaser: The game publisher acknowledged using generative AI content in Crazy Taxi World Tour, which launches in 2027.
cards.body:
Sega confirmed that its upcoming Crazy Taxi World Tour contains generative AI content and issued a response addressing the use of the technology. The game represents a reboot of the arcade series and is scheduled for release in 2027. The announcement revealed that the game reunites with the punk rock band that provided music for the 1999 arcade original.

The disclosure prompted discussion about the role of AI-generated content in game development. Critics questioned the necessity of using generative AI for a Crazy Taxi title. Sega announced the game during the Xbox Games Showcase, positioning it as a continuation of the franchise that has been dormant for years.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: The next entry in the role-playing game series was officially revealed with a toxic green color scheme and graveyard visuals.
cards.body:
Atlus confirmed Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest 2026. The announcement came as a brief teaser, officially revealing the long-awaited next entry in the series.

The revelation followed months of leaked images circulating online. Sega had attempted to remove these leaked materials from the internet in the days before the official announcement. Persona 6 joins Final Fantasy VII Remake's conclusion as major Japanese RPG announcements from this year's Summer Game Fest.

hero.headline: Nelly Korda wins first U.S. Women's Open title
hero.body:
World number one Nelly Kord captured her first U.S. Women's Open championship, holding off England's Charley Hull by a single stroke at Riviera Country Club. The victory represents the fourth major title of Kord's career and marks the fulfillment of a longtime goal for the American golfer.

Kord secured the win with a steady two-under 69 in the final round. The decisive moment came on the 18th green, where her second putt from just over two feet caught the edge of the cup. The ball toured nearly half the circumference of the hole before dropping in, giving Kord the one-shot victory she needed.

The tournament also saw Gaby Lopez finish within one stroke of the champion, making for an exceptionally tight competition at the finish. Kord's ability to maintain composure through the closing holes proved crucial to her success.

This marks Kord's second consecutive major victory, extending her recent dominance in professional women's golf. Her performance throughout the week demonstrated the consistency that has established her as the top-ranked player in the sport.

For Hull, the runner-up finish represents another near miss in pursuit of a first major championship. The English golfer has repeatedly contended in the biggest tournaments on the women's golf calendar but continues to search for her breakthrough victory at the major level.

Kord's triumph at Riviera Country Club continues a strong period for American players in major championships. The victory adds another chapter to her family's notable golfing legacy.

The U.S. Women's Open had remained the one major title missing from Kord's resume before this week. Having already collected three other major championships, winning at Riviera filled the final gap in her major championship collection.

Kord's path to victory showcased the mental strength required to succeed in major championships. Her ability to execute crucial shots down the stretch and handle the pressure of a close final round separated her from the competition.

The win comes as part of what has been a successful period for Kord on the women's golf circuit. Her status as the world's top-ranked player now comes with the validation of major championship success across all the sport's most prestigious events.

For the women's golf world, Kord's dominance shows little sign of slowing. Her combination of consistent play and the ability to deliver in high-pressure moments makes her the player to beat in upcoming tournaments.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho set to return as Real Madrid head coach
cards.teaser: Jose Mourinho is expected to be confirmed as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president.
cards.body:
Jose Mourinho will be formally announced as Real Madrid's new head coach following Florentino Perez's re-election as club president. Perez secured 65% of the vote in the club's first competitive election in 20 years, defeating challenger Enrique Riquelme who received 35% support from the 33,555 members who voted.

Real Madrid will pay Benfica a €15 million release fee to bring Mourinho to the club. The Portuguese coach's appointment represents a new direction for the Spanish giants as they prepare for the upcoming season under Perez's continued leadership through 2030.

cards.headline: Crusaders suffer record 134-0 defeat in rugby league
cards.teaser: The Crusaders endured the biggest defeat in the 131-year history of rugby league's top two divisions, losing 134-0.
cards.body:
The Crusaders suffered a record 134-0 defeat, the largest loss in the top two divisions of rugby league across its 131-year history. The scoreline stands as an unprecedented result in professional rugby league competition.

The magnitude of this defeat marks a significant milestone in the sport's elite tiers, surpassing all previous losses recorded at the highest levels of rugby league.

cards.headline: Denny Hamlin wins third race of 2026 at Michigan
cards.teaser: Denny Hamlin captured his third victory of the 2026 NASCAR season with a win at Michigan International Speedway.
cards.body:
Denny Hamlin secured victory at Michigan International Speedway, claiming his third win of the 2026 NASCAR season. The race featured a red flag stoppage following a serious crash between Christopher Bell and Chase Elliott that damaged the track wall.

Hamlin had earlier captured the pole position at Michigan, though his car suffered damage before the main event. Despite the setback, he recovered to dominate the FireKeepers Casino 400 and extend his successful season.

cards.headline: Alexander Zverev wins first Grand Slam title at French Open
cards.teaser: Alexander Zverev captured his first Grand Slam championship with a victory at the French Open, ending his wait for a major title.
cards.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Italy's Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in the final. The second seed's victory came in his fourth major final appearance. After Cobolli missed an overhead on the second championship point, Zverev collapsed to his back in an emotional display.

Zverev had previously won at Masters 1000 events, the ATP Finals twice, and claimed Olympic gold in Tokyo 2020, but major championships had eluded him until now. His breakthrough triumph concluded one of the most chaotic men's Grand Slam tournaments in recent memory.

cards.headline: Karl-Anthony Towns leads Knicks in first NBA Finals appearance
cards.teaser: Karl-Anthony Towns has delivered strong two-way play for the Knicks in his first NBA Finals, helping New York win Game 2.
cards.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns is rewriting his career narrative with impactful two-way play in his first NBA Finals appearance. The Knicks center has been particularly effective defending Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, earning praise as a key factor in New York's Game 2 victory.

After the win, Towns paid tribute to his late mother, marking an emotional moment in his Finals debut. His performance has generated discussion about how his playoff success might influence the Knicks' future plans and potential pursuit of other stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo.

cards.headline: Tarik Skubal pitches five scoreless innings in rehab start
cards.teaser: Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal threw five scoreless innings for West Michigan in his first rehab appearance, just one month after surgery.
cards.body:
Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal made a successful return to the mound, pitching five scoreless innings in a rehab start with the West Michigan Whitecaps. The outing came just one month after the left-hander underwent surgery, marking a remarkably quick recovery timeline.

Skubal struck out multiple batters while showing no apparent limitations from his recent procedure. After the game, he expressed confidence in his ability to return to form, saying he was focused on being himself on the mound. The Tigers are monitoring his progress as they work toward his return to the major league rotation.

hero.headline: Qween Jean Becomes First Openly Trans Person to Win Tony Award
hero.body:
Qween Jean achieved a significant milestone in theater history at the 79th Tony Awards, becoming the first openly transgender person to win the prestigious honor. Jean's award recognized her work in costume design for the Broadway production of Cats.

During her acceptance speech, Jean reflected on the broader significance of her win. "The world right now is deeply, deeply combating so many ailments, and we know as a society that when we come together, we can make real, permanent change," she said while addressing the audience at the ceremony.

The Tony Awards annually recognize excellence across Broadway theater, honoring achievements in acting, directing, writing, and design. Jean's victory in the costume design category represents an important moment for transgender representation among mainstream theater award winners. Her costume designs helped shape the visual experience of Cats throughout its Broadway run.

The 79th Tony Awards ceremony showcased multiple notable achievements across the theater community. The musical Schmigadoon also made headlines at the event, winning the Best Musical award. The win contributed to Apple TV becoming the fastest streaming service to achieve EGOT status, the entertainment industry's most prestigious honor requiring wins at the Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Awards.

Jean's historic achievement comes during a period when Broadway continues to expand recognition of diverse artists and creators working behind the scenes and on stage. The Tony Awards have gradually increased representation across various categories throughout their decades of honoring Broadway excellence. Each milestone in this progression reflects the evolving nature of the theater industry and its commitment to acknowledging talent across different backgrounds and identities.

The costume design category has long been central to Broadway's visual storytelling. Designers in this field work to create clothing and visual elements that enhance character development and support a production's overall artistic vision. Jean's recognition by the Tony Awards validates the essential contributions that designers make to successful theatrical productions.

The recognition of Jean's work underscores how Broadway continues to evolve as a creative community. Major awards ceremonies like the Tonys serve as important markers of industry values and priorities. By honoring Jean's talent and contributions, the awards ceremony acknowledged both her individual achievement and the broader importance of inclusion within professional theater.

Jean's win joins a growing number of achievements that demonstrate increasing visibility for transgender artists in major entertainment industries. As Broadway continues to produce diverse stories and employ diverse talent, awards recognition becomes an important validation of these contributions to the art form and to cultural conversations happening on and off stage.

cards.headline: Schmigadoon Wins Best Musical at Tony Awards
cards.teaser: The Apple TV-backed stage adaptation of the streaming series won the top award at the 79th Tony Awards.
cards.body:
Schmigadoon! claimed the Tony Award for Best Musical at the 2026 ceremony. The stage production, based on the Apple TV series, marked a significant milestone for the streaming service, which had previously canceled the original show before backing its Broadway adaptation.

The win helped Apple TV achieve "studio EGOT" status—having won an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony across different productions. Cinco Paul won Best Book of a Musical for Schmigadoon. During the acceptance speech, a producer acknowledged Apple TV's decision to cancel the series, adding a pointed note to the celebration.

cards.headline: John Lithgow Sets Tony Record as Oldest Male Acting Winner at 80
cards.teaser: The actor won for his role in Giant, surpassing a record that had stood since 2000.
cards.body:
John Lithgow became the oldest man to win a competitive acting Tony Award at age 80 for his performance in the play Giant. The actor surpassed the previous record held by Roy Dotrice, who won at age 77 for featured actor in a play in 2000.

Lithgow's win also marked a 53-year span between his first Tony win and his latest. With this third Tony Award, Lithgow has now won in three of the four acting categories across his Broadway career. He attended the ceremony with his wife of 44 years, Mary Yeager.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Tops Box Office With $55 Million Opening
cards.teaser: The R-rated comedy revival outperformed Masters of the Universe during its opening weekend.
cards.body:
Scary Movie led the domestic box office with a $55 million opening weekend, continuing a recent trend of successful low-budget films. The legacy sequel parodies other legacy sequels while returning politically incorrect humor to mainstream theaters.

The film defeated Masters of the Universe, which also debuted during the weekend. Scary Movie earned $105 million globally in its opening, marking a revival for R-rated comedies at the box office. The performance adds to a streak of low-budget films outperforming bigger-budget competitors in recent weeks.

cards.headline: Colony Holds Top Spot at South Korean Box Office
cards.teaser: The local action-horror film retained first place during its third weekend in theaters.
cards.body:
Colony remained at the top of the South Korean box office during the June 5-7 weekend, generating $4 million from 603,868 admissions. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the film captured a 44.35% revenue share during its third weekend.

The action-horror thriller continued to dominate despite new competition. Wild Sing debuted strong during the same weekend, but Colony maintained its leading position among local audiences. The film's performance demonstrates continued audience interest in Korean-produced genre films.

---

Note: The provided source material about World Food Photography Awards is unrelated to this box office story, so the original card text has been retained unchanged.

cards.headline: Dear You Leads China Box Office for Second Weekend
cards.teaser: The low-budget family drama earned $17 million and has reached a cumulative total of $238.5 million.
cards.body:
Dear You dominated the China box office during the June 5-7 weekend, securing RMB 115.3 million ($17 million) according to data from Artisan Gateway. Directed by Lan Hongchun and starring Li Sitong and Wang Yantong, the Jinant Film TV production has reached a cumulative total of $238.5 million.

The low-budget family drama held its leading position against new releases including Masters of the Universe, which also debuted during the weekend. The film has become what industry observers describe as a cultural phenomenon, continuing to draw audiences despite multiple weeks in theaters.

cards.headline: Pink Opens Tony Awards With Lady Marmalade Performance
cards.teaser: The host kicked off the ceremony with a Broadway-sized reinvention featuring Megan Thee Stallion and Neil Patrick Harris.
cards.body:
Pink hosted the 79th Tony Awards at Radio City Music Hall, launching the ceremony with a high-energy rendition of "Lady Marmalade." The opening number brought together an ensemble cast of performers including Neil Patrick Harris, Megan Thee Stallion, Lea Michele, Dylan Mulvaney, June Squibb, and Shoshana Bean.

The reworked Moulin Rouge musical number set an energetic tone for the evening's celebration of Broadway. Pink's performance kicked off a night that saw major wins including John Lithgow and Lesley Manville taking home acting honors, while Schmigadoon! claimed the Best Musical award.

hero.headline: Treasury plans to use Iranian assets to rebuild Gulf nations
hero.teaser: The Treasury Department intends to redirect Iranian assets to help Gulf allies recover from war damage.
hero.body:
The Treasury Department is considering removing sanctions on Iranian oil currently stranded on tankers at sea as part of efforts to control rising energy prices, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Thursday.

Bessent said the administration may lift sanctions on approximately 140 million barrels of Iranian crude in the coming days. He described the move as a temporary measure to address supply disruptions caused by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

"In essence, we will be using the Iranian barrels against the Iranians to keep the price down for the next 10 to 14 days as we continue this campaign," Bessent said during an appearance on Fox Business Network.

The oil stranded on tankers represents roughly 10 to 14 days of supply that Iran had been directing toward China. Oil prices have exceeded $100 per barrel for much of the past two weeks following Iran's actions blocking the critical shipping route and attacking vessels.

According to a source familiar with Treasury planning, the administration could implement a waiver similar to one previously used for Russian oil. Such a waiver would allow sales of crude already at sea within a limited timeframe. The source indicated that diverting oil already intended for China into broader global markets could help address supply shortages and reduce Iran's ability to leverage the strait closure.

The Treasury is also pursuing other measures to increase oil supplies. Bessent said the department would release additional stocks from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve beyond last week's coordinated G7 release of 400 million barrels. He emphasized that while the administration would not intervene in financial futures markets, it would focus on increasing physical supplies to compensate for the 10 to 14 million barrel-per-day deficit caused by the strait's closure.

However, experts have questioned whether this approach serves American interests. David Tannenbaum from Blackstone Compliance Services told the BBC that allowing Iran to sell oil could inadvertently strengthen the regime's financial position.

"Essentially, we're allowing Iran to sell oil, which could then be used to fund the war effort," Tannenbaum said.

Alex Zerden, founder of Capitol Peak Strategies, expressed similar concerns to the New York Times, arguing that Iran would likely profit from the sales.

"Iran will likely profit from these sales, thereby providing more money to fund its regime, the war and its proxies," Zerden said, adding that he doubted the measure would provide meaningful market reassurance.

Bessent's proposal represents a short-term approach to address immediate energy market disruptions, though analysts question its long-term effectiveness and potential unintended consequences.

cards.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iranian missile attack
cards.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to strike Iran in response to a missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy.
cards.body:
President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to strike Iran in response to a missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the call. The conversation came after Iran launched missiles at Israel earlier in the day, the first such attack since an April ceasefire.

The president's effort to restrain an Israeli response reflects his administration's concern that further military escalation could derail ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran. Trump spoke with Axios before the call and indicated he planned to urge Netanyahu to hold off on retaliation. Despite the intervention, Israel proceeded with strikes on military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning local time, according to the Israel Defense Forces.

The Israeli strikes mark a significant escalation in tensions between the two nations and represent the first time Israel has struck Iran since the April ceasefire. The IDF said the strikes targeted military facilities in retaliation for the Iranian missile attack. The exchange of fire threatens to unravel the diplomatic efforts underway between Washington and Tehran.

The Trump administration has been working to negotiate with Iran while managing the fallout from the renewed conflict. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is planning to use Iranian assets to assist Gulf allies in rebuilding after damage from the war, according to a CBS News report citing a source aware of Bessent's thinking. The Treasury Department intends to redirect these funds to support regional partners affected by Iranian military action.

Trump has defended his handling of the situation against critics who say the conflict contradicts his campaign promise of no new wars. The president dismissed the notion that launching military action against Iran betrayed his 2024 campaign message. The ongoing negotiations and military tensions present a complex challenge for the administration as it seeks to manage both diplomatic engagement and regional security concerns.

cards.headline: Israel conducts strikes on Iranian military sites
cards.teaser: The Israeli Air Force hit military targets in central and western Iran following Tehran's missile attack.
cards.body:
The Israeli Air Force struck military targets in central and western Iran on Monday morning, according to the Israel Defense Forces. The strikes came in response to Iranian missile attacks on Israel.

The exchange marked an escalation in tensions between the two countries and threatened to widen the regional conflict. The strikes occurred despite an appeal from U.S. President Donald Trump to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu urging restraint. Yemen's Houthi rebels warned they would target Israel-affiliated ships in the Red Sea amid the escalating tensions.

cards.headline: Trump defends Iran military action against campaign promise criticism
cards.teaser: President Trump rejected suggestions that the war with Iran contradicts his no new wars pledge.
cards.body:
President Trump is rejecting criticism that military action against Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign promise to avoid new wars. The president addressed the concern as tensions with Iran escalated.

During his campaign for the White House, Trump emphasized avoiding new military conflicts abroad. The current situation with Iran has raised questions about whether the administration's actions align with that campaign message.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges UFC fight planned for White House lawn
cards.teaser: Legal filing contends the Trump administration's authorization of the June 14 event was unlawful.
cards.body:
A lawsuit seeks to stop a UFC fight scheduled for the White House South Lawn on June 14, the president's birthday. The legal filing argues that the Trump administration's authorization of the event violated the law.

The lawsuit challenges the use of White House grounds for the mixed martial arts event. The complaint raises questions about the appropriate use of government property for commercial sporting events.

cards.headline: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary
cards.teaser: Haaland could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Haaland, who previously served as a U.S. representative from New Mexico before joining the Biden Cabinet, secured the nomination to run in the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She will face the Republican nominee in the general election race to lead New Mexico.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead California gubernatorial primary results
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead in early returns to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra lead in early results from California's gubernatorial primary. Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer and Republican Chad Bianco are also competing for their party's nominations to replace Gov. Gavin Newsom.

California uses a top-two primary system, meaning the two candidates with the most votes regardless of party will advance to the general election. The race to lead the nation's most populous state has attracted multiple high-profile candidates from both parties.
